newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gasoline weaker.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gasoline weaker.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday, with gasoline easier and high sulphur fuel oil steady, traders said.
Gasoline lost $1-2 a tonne in response to weaker U.S gasoline futures and slack local demand.

Traders said the market looked to be heading southwards, making buyers more relaxed. Eurograde cargoes were pegged around $220 cif Med. Bearish Euroil stock data released on Monday which showed a build of 4.5 million barrels in December also contributed to the weaker sentiment.
Naphtha also lost ground in line with easier crude levels.
Traders said activity was very thin with Petchem buyers looking to push their requirements as far forward as possible. Full range dipped $2 or so to around $229 cif.

Gas oil was quiet. Heating oil demand was minimal, with only two buyers seen. Outright prices fell as futures were pulled lower by milder European temperatures and a slump on U.S. crude and products markets.
Traders saw Russian steady to slightly higher at cif high +2.50 cif Genoa, with bids at +$2/2.20 and offers around +$3.
High sulphur fuel oil held steady supported by good demand for bunker fuels.
Physical high sulphur cracked cargoes valued around $120 a tonne cif Med with non-Isab material $2 higher.
Low sulphur fuel oil was assessed steady to firmer but trade was thin with traders awaiting fresh demand from Italain state utility Enel.
"I think prices will ultimately go higher but the market is really waiting for Enel to come back in again," one trader said.
Traders said the market was also still awaiting news of a Turkish tender for 45,000-50,000 tonnes of low sulphur cracked fuel oil, for delivery at the end of January.
